c11_biotech_cbse_02_006: A burst lysosome won't digest the cell — its enzymes stall at neutral pH and the membrane resists them. Check: what pH do they need?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_007: ATP is made at the inner membrane by ATP synthase, not loose in the matrix. Check: where does the proton flow turn?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_008: Chlorophyll isn't one pigment — a, b and carotenoids each catch different light. Check: why does chromatography show bands?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_009: The envelope doesn't always dissolve — many fungi run a closed mitosis with it intact. Check: is every mitosis 'open'?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_010: Svedbergs don't add — 30S plus 50S makes 70S because shape counts, not just mass. Check: what does S measure?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_011: Don't trust the names — microtubules are the thickest (25 nm), microfilaments the thinnest (6). Check: which is 10 nm?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_012: Peroxisomes aren't lysosomes — they oxidise with catalase while lysosomes hydrolyse in acid. Check: which buds from the ER?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_001: D/L marks the C-5 configuration; alpha/beta marks the anomeric carbon — neither means rotation direction. Check: which carbon decides D or L?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_002: The peptide bond links alpha-carboxyl to alpha-amino — never to an R-group. Check: which amino acid isn't chiral?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_003: Helix H-bonds run along the backbone, not between R-groups — and disulfides aren't 'secondary'. Check: which atoms hydrogen-bond?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_004: 'Lipid' is a solubility label, not a shape — the membrane is built from phospholipids, not triglycerides. Check: which lipid lines the cell?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_005: Not all steroids are hormones — cholesterol is mostly a membrane part and a precursor. Check: name a non-hormone steroid.
c11_biotech_cbse_03_006: The strands join by thousands of cooperative H-bonds plus stacking — weak singly, strong together. Check: what holds each strand internally?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_007: RNA isn't single-stranded DNA — its 2'-OH makes it fold, react and even catalyse. Check: what can rRNA do that DNA can't?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_008: 5' and 3' number the sugar's carbons, not the phosphate. Check: which carbon carries the free OH?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_009: Water resists heating because energy first breaks intermolecular H-bonds — not because it has three atoms. Check: which bond is ~20 kJ/mol?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_010: Vitamins don't give you calories — they're cofactors that let enzymes release energy. Check: is it fuel or a helper?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_001: Class an enzyme by the reaction it runs, not by its name — hexokinase is a transferase. Check: what bond chemistry happens?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_002: Even a 'lock and key' fit strains the substrate's bonds toward the transition state. Check: does the bound substrate stay unstrained?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_003: Induced fit isn't a floppy enzyme — the substrate stabilises a rare ready shape. Check: was the shape present before binding?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_004: Km isn't the same as Kd, and low Km isn't always better — compare kcat/Km. Check: what gives half Vmax?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_005: Heat doesn't make enzymes 'tired' — it unfolds them for good, and extreme pH can too. Check: does activity return on cooling?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_006: Km is the substrate level giving half Vmax — not the level for Vmax, and not always Kd. Check: what's v at [S] = Km?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_007: A pure non-competitive inhibitor drops Vmax but leaves Km alone — it binds E and ES equally. Check: does Km shift?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_008: An allosteric inhibitor can raise K0.5 while Vmax stays put — the sigmoid just slides right. Check: did the plateau drop?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_009: Cofactors and coenzymes differ — FAD comes from riboflavin (B2) and CoA from pantothenate (B5). Check: which vitamin makes FAD?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_010: Ribozymes aren't primitive leftovers — the ribosome's RNA core catalyses peptide bonds superbly. Check: what makes the peptide bond?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_001: 'Resting phase' is a misnomer — interphase is the busiest stretch, with its own checkpoints. Check: when does DNA double?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_002: After S phase you still have 46 chromosomes — each just carries two sister chromatids. Check: count centromeres, not chromatids.
c11_biotech_cbse_05_003: Fibres don't push chromosomes to the plate — kinetochores pull from both poles until tension balances. Check: what moves the chromosome?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_004: Mitosis adds cells; it doesn't enlarge them — and repair uses the same machinery. Check: hyperplasia or hypertrophy?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_005: Crossing over swaps non-sister chromatids of homologues — and no new S phase precedes meiosis II. Check: sisters or non-sisters?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_006: Meiosis II isn't plain mitosis — crossing over already made sisters different, so four gametes differ. Check: are sisters identical?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_007: Crossing over belongs to Prophase I and assortment to Metaphase I — homologues are gone by II. Check: are homologues still paired?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_008: Apoptosis is an orderly, ATP-driven shutdown — swelling, bursting and inflammation mean necrosis. Check: do caspases run?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_009: Apoptotic blebs are active remodelling — a necrotic cell swells and leaks instead. Check: is ATP still flowing?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_010: Cyclin binding alone doesn't switch a CDK on — it needs CAK's phosphate and Cdc25's cleanup. Check: is the T-loop phosphorylated?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_001: Mendel picked peas for control — selfing flowers, clear-cut traits and true-breeding lines. Check: could he force a cross?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_002: Dominant doesn't delete recessive — the allele hides in F1 and returns in F2. Check: can two talls give a dwarf?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_003: Segregation is homologues parting in meiosis I — a test cross gives 1:1 only for a heterozygote. Check: is the parent Tt or TT?
